title: Conserving Water:
status: draft: written 18 Nov 2026 offline for Grade 6 Agriculture; not yet checked by a CBC Agriculture teacher; not loaded by the live tutor
notes: Dig one sunken bed and a few shallow (zai-like) pits in the school garden; compare the soil moisture with a flat bed after a week without rain.

skills.key_step: The child says which seedbeds keep soil moisture (sunken beds and shallow pits in dry places, mulched beds) and how they are made (dug below ground level, edges raised, manure mixed in, mulched), and that raised beds suit wet places.

floor.prerequisite: Knows ways of conserving water in a garden.
floor.question: Name a way to conserve water in a garden.

representations: a cross-section drawing of sunken, flat and raised beds
steps: Dry place: sink the bed or dig pits.
Raise the edges to hold water.
Wet place: raise the bed instead.
contexts: the school garden in a dry spell

board.do: Draw a sunken bed and a raised bed in cross-section.
Ask which holds rain water in a dry place.
Draw water held in the sunken bed.

misconceptions.ask: Which seedbed keeps moisture best in a dry place?
misconceptions.repair: Pour water on a raised and a sunken bed and watch which keeps it.

misconceptions.ask: Which seedbed suits a very wet place?
misconceptions.repair: Pour a lot of water on both beds.

misconceptions.ask: What does mulch do on a seedbed?
misconceptions.repair: Cover one bed with dry grass and leave one bare in the sun.

misconceptions.ask: What is put in a shallow planting pit before planting?
misconceptions.repair: Grow two pits, one with manure; compare after a month.

checks.question: Which seedbed suits a dry area?
checks.answer: a sunken bed or shallow pits

checks.question: Why mulch a sunken bed?
checks.answer: to stop the water drying up
